safety_line: Toxic enough to make a pet vomit or act ill if eaten; call your vet if that happens. Its defensive foam can also irritate skin and eyes — wear gloves if you handle it.
traits: Huge — up to 3 inches — slow-moving, and can barely fly
Adults yellow-orange-red with black wing edges; nymphs are black with a yellow/orange/red stripe
Marches across yards and driveways in early summer, often in groups
Hisses and spreads its wings when threatened, sometimes spraying a foul-smelling defensive foam

look_alikes.difference: Lubbers are heavy-bodied, slow, and can barely fly; katydids are slender, leaf-green, and jump or fly readily.
look_alikes.next_photo: A side-on photo showing body shape and wing length relative to the body.

copy.what_it_means: Its bold colors are a warning label — lubbers carry chemicals toxic enough that most predators spit them out, and a dog or cat that eats one can get sick. They chew ornamentals but rarely at damaging scale in a typical yard; the bigger concern where pets have yard access is keeping them from eating one.
copy.fact: Its colors are a warning label — lubbers are toxic enough that most predators spit them back out, and the same chemicals can make a pet ill if it eats one.
copy.blurb: They chew ornamentals but rarely at damaging scale in yards. Keep pets from eating them, and wear gloves if you remove any by hand.

tech_notes: Not a lawn-turf pest; ornamental nibbling only. If hand removal is needed, use gloves — the defensive foam can irritate skin/eyes and the insect is toxic if a pet eats it. Spot treatment on high-value ornamentals if numerous.

traits: Raised, meandering surface tunnels like mini mole runs in turf
Spongy turf that peels up easily where tunneling is heavy
Velvety brown insect with shovel-shaped front legs, up to about 3.5 cm
Loud trilling or nasal calling song from burrows on spring evenings

look_alikes.difference: Mole cricket tunnels are narrow, meandering ridges made by an insect; eastern mole tunnels are wider ridges made by a furry mammal, not an insect.
look_alikes.next_photo: A wide shot of the tunnel width and any entry holes, plus a close-up if the animal is seen.

copy.what_it_means: Tunneling severs turf roots, so small areas usually recover on their own while spreading tunnels are worth treating. Males shape their burrows like megaphones to amplify their calling song across the neighborhood.
copy.fact: Males sing from burrows shaped like megaphones to amplify the call across the neighborhood.
copy.blurb: Tunneling severs roots — small areas recover, spreading tunnels need treatment.

tech_notes: Soap-flush test confirms presence/density. Peak egg-lay/hatch spring; treat young nymphs for best control.
